title: November 17 — toward Synthetic Qualia
summary: Five newly reviewed Nov 17 repositories (census 648→653), connected to the already-curated Nov 16 Qualia chapter. Distinguishes inherited two-form circuit, addressed two-hop relay, apical rule reversal, fusion in WaveCortex, and paper-only SyntheticQualia. Sources report positive preregistered gates and negative scalar comparisons; not independently rerun here. No evidence for phenomenal experience.

nodes.claim: Unifies content, residue, latched clocks and the two-form imagined relay in one learned A→B→C wave body.
nodes.survived: Seven pre-registered checks pass in 32-body matched conditions. Imagined C sign is right in 32/32. Weaker A→B gives ratio 0.65 (Bayes 0.57; certain regen 0.93). Noisy-B contradiction gives C 0.035. A kernel built from the linear grid reportedly runs 55× faster and retrains 48 old bodies to 8e−8.
nodes.killed: Event locations, timing, calibration and perception/imagination mode are supplied. Eyes-closed/own-link ratios 0.97 and 1.02 are medians, not zero per-body error; learned B→C is only 0.86–0.90 of Bayes. No wave accuracy advantage or subjective-experience test.
nodes.era: November 17: from shared prediction to synthetic qualia

nodes.claim: Tests a four-event wave body, A→imagined B→imagined C→D, with explicit writer addressing, clocks and amplitude fitting.
nodes.survived: Addressed design preserves measured learned-link amplitudes in 96/96 bodies; both relay cuts abolish D, contradictory real evidence reverses it, and weakening either link reduces D by factors 0.570 and 0.541 (Bayes 0.571).
nodes.killed: Writer channels, event slots and a second training-only gain fit are supplied. Strong-link world fails amplitude and full-waveform criteria: 0.135 absolute error vs 0.023 scalar; mixed field shows 21–42% cross-talk error. It does not infer addresses itself.

nodes.claim: Adds a multiplicative apical W+gV rule gate to WaveComputer's verified fade-clock wave machine.
nodes.survived: Five registered tests pass in 32 bodies: stable F and reversing R cues sort into W and V (31/32); apical cut leaves fixed F at 1.00, reversing cues at 0.49; inferred-rule accuracy 0.86; first-unseen-cue transfer 0.92 vs plastic 0.08.
nodes.killed: A single shared g, its starting sign, cue labels and rates are supplied. Only one binary rule reversal is tested; scalar-copy error 0.069 beats wave 0.105. Cortical lesion comparison is qualitative, not a claim of biological identity.

nodes.claim: Fuses WaveComputer's two-form imagined B relay with ApicalRuleReversalMachine's fast surprise-driven context g along the same A→B→C chain.
nodes.survived: All six pre-registered checks pass with inherited constants and no retuning across 32 bodies: links sort gated into V vs fixed into W in 32/32; imagined C accuracy 0.87; transfer 0.79 vs plastic 0.08; apical cut makes the imagined chain 0.50 but preserves fixed real-B link at 1.00; belief-amplitude correlation 0.79.
nodes.killed: Two-form slope against ideal is 0.64. Scalar model error 0.049 beats wave 0.091 in 32/32. One shared g, clock calibrations, geometry and event slots are given; no object permanence or consciousness established.

nodes.claim: README-format paper defines a functional synthetic quale, distinguishing it from phenomenal qualia, and synthesizes the preceding predictive experiments.
nodes.survived: Organizes small-toy findings as six tested functional properties Q1–Q6: shared prediction, hidden causes, perception/imagination reuse, graded certainty, state revision under frozen weights and causal meaning. Identifies Q7 hidden-object persistence, Q8 multisensory binding and Q9 counterfactual sensing as untested.
nodes.killed: A research synthesis, not an additional trained body or independent replication. Q1–Q6 occur across different toy settings, not one persistent multimodal world. No assay establishes subjective experience; the label is functional, not a consciousness claim.

motifs.title: Context-sensitive imagination carries content and belief
motifs.description: Two-form relay, slow W/V weights and fast inferred g combine to pass an imagined event through a context-dependent chain, with residual-based learning and graded confidence but imperfect calibration.

motifs.title: Linear wave transport costs accuracy on these symbolic chains
motifs.description: An impulse-response Green's function is an exact representation of the linear wave carrier, but scalar copies of the task algorithm beat the wave bodies. This is a task-specific negative, not an impossibility result for spatial wave computation.

motifs.title: Functional shared prediction is testable; felt experience is not shown
motifs.description: The paper organizes toy tests of Q1–Q6 while leaving Q7 hidden-object persistence, Q8 causal multisensory binding and Q9 counterfactual sensing open. Its functional definition is not proof of phenomenal qualia.
